newsitem.title: UK: British manufacturing output falls sharply in May.
newsitem.headline: British manufacturing output falls sharply in May.

text.p: British manufacturing output fell 1.1 percent in May over April, official data showed on Monday, raising concerns among analysts that the strong pound was hitting exporters hard.
Industrial output fell 0.9 percent in May over April and 0.2 percent year-on-year. Manufacturing output was 1.0 percent higher on a year on year basis in May after a 2.7 percent rise in April.

The Bank of England meets this week to discuss monetary policy and is widely expected to increase interest rates from 6.50 percent. Last week's budget failed to dampen consumer spending sufficiently, many analysts believe.
Analysts said the output data should give the bank food for thought but they still expected rates to rise, underpinning the strength of the pound.
"The pound we know is too strong and is likely to head even higher. These manufacturing figures should set the alarm bells ringing," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
Sterling dropped more than a pfennig on the figures to below 2.94 marks. Shares were down but little affected.
